question: Which independently sampled reef regions yield at least two separate fixed Method-1 transects in the same month in successive years, so species t-to-t+1 sampled detection changes could be evaluated without inventing unsampled zeros?

authoritative_source.official: AODN IMOS National Reef Monitoring Network

method_1_rule: Only a survey whose original comma-delimited numeric methods field contains integer 1; a value of 11 or 13 does not count as 1. Never infer method from other codes.
event_unit: unique survey_id; duplicate IDs removed before counting. A distinct survey ID approximates one physical transect, not one independent site or breeding population.
site_unit: RLS+country+area+location+site_code trimmed casefold; stable if all observed 11-column record coordinates vary <=0.01 degrees latitude and longitude
target_unit: same RLS site+calendar month in consecutive years with at least 2 distinct Method 1 survey IDs in both
study_precondition: Fixed 10 RLS source groups already passed survey method-agnostic frame v1.260; no post-outcome source group selection

outputs.per_10_group: survey+site+years+strict pairs only with source methods+Method1 categories and counts; NO survey_id, site lat/lon, site_code or fish taxa
outputs.aggregate: strict pairs all 10, qualification counts and program/season coverage

next_step: If 2+ physically independent reef localities retain method1 matched sampling, freeze source-independent geographic/archipelago groupings and pilot/holdout before fish species observations; otherwise STOP rescue via lowering thresholds.
